Review of 0828b759bb88, fb30c47923ac, and 49a3880621e4 (2026-10-18).

decode.sh is a 51-byte shell snippet. echo reads the caller's h variable;
xxd -r -p decodes hex, then two Base64 stages decode it into sh stdin.
No h assignment, payload, network operation, or hostile effect is present.
BENIGN is the evidence-limited verdict; layered execution remains suspicious.
Neither decoder composition nor multiple encodings makes this a polyglot.

Both PE files have the same x86 loader text except a patched call at 0x401f8f.
Rizin disassembly traces CRT entry 0x402674 to WinMain 0x401cb0, which selects
installation modes using 0x404120 (3 in these images). Mode 3 calls 0x401900:
generate a GUID, write HKLM Active Setup Installed Components\GUID StubPath,
read its own image, patch the copy, write a GUID-named executable and launch it.
This branch writes persistence before any dependency on a working DLL payload.

Other retained branches extract resource DLL/101 (0x402460 -> 0x4023c0),
replace LanmanServer\Parameters ServiceDLL (0x401260), or create an auto-start
service (0x401fd0 -> CreateServiceA with dwStartType 2 at 0x4021cc).
0x401150 creates an IE/notepad/calc host selected by configuration, allocates
remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA, and passes
that address plus the remote path to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401390 gets its module path, converts it to a short path, builds COMSPEC
/c del <self> > nul, and starts the shell. These are concrete persistence,
service hijack, injection and self-removal code paths, rather than API guesses.
StormAttack identity is corroborated by the server/welcome banner pair and
the matching loader behavior. No observed code supports WannaCry ransomware
or Remcos identification from the collector-assigned names.

fb30c47923ac has an entirely zero-filled .rsrc and ten extra zero-filled
sections. The loader cannot extract its missing resource payload. Do not
describe successful payload deployment, network control, or encryption.
Its retained self-copy/persistence and cleanup code supports MALICIOUS.

49a3880621e4 embeds a 39936-byte DLL at 0x5060. Its .data is mostly zero,
and entry RVA 0x741a maps to erased bytes at child offset 0x681a. Surviving
STORM protocol/HTTP strings do not prove a working DDoS or RAT payload.
The patched jump at 0x401f8f leads to 0x40f000, calls self-delete, runs
repeated dec/inc CH, self-moves, and self-exchanges, then jumps back to
0x401f94 at 0x40f40e. This is a junk-code detour, not encrypted shellcode.
The existing two suspicious filler traits accurately describe two of its
padding forms. Its persistence and injection loader code supports MALICIOUS.

YAML changes: decoder-only observations become notable. The old polyglot
sequence moves to data/decode/multiple-encoding with an evidence-level name.
The direct Base64-to-shell operation moves to process/create/shell/pipeline,
preserving its matcher and exclusions. It replaces the weaker unbound Base64
output matcher in that leaf; scope gains github-actions and makefile.
The suspicious objective now binds two decode stages and sh in one pipeline,
so unrelated nearby commands cannot satisfy it. Update exact consumers;
remove the redundant hostile Makefile consumer: the recipe name plus an
encoded pipeline proves no tampering with a legitimate build input. The
suspicious double-decode-to-sh objective still covers Makefile recipes.
The stacking matcher additionally recognizes xxd -r -p as the first stage.
The double-decode atom also covers the existing github-actions consumer scope.
Only the two shell observations are moved; no new taxonomy leaf is introduced.
Decoder and shell directory selectors still select the same capability kinds;
no generic capability was moved into an intent tier. Historic review snapshots
retain their original IDs. check.py supplies positive and near-miss controls.

atomscan and cleave facts ran on all three full sample paths before edits.
Re-scans must retain 0 hostile / at most 1 suspicious for decode.sh and four
hostile loader traits for each PE. No dependency package is involved.
The supplied Triage reports were inaccessible through the web tool; verdicts
derive from the bytes, not external engine counts or family labels.

Verification: all eight check.py controls passed. Final atomscan results:
0828b759bb88: 0 hostile, 1 suspicious. fb30c47923ac: 4 hostile, 1 suspicious.
49a3880621e4: 4 hostile, 3 suspicious; embedded damaged DLL: 0 hostile, 0 suspicious.
Judgment markers were written beside all three original samples.
